CLAUDE.md

Source: CLAUDE.md

This file provides guidance to Claude Code (claude.ai/code) when working with code in this repository.

What this is

zulm builds computation graphs of tensors in R, runs them on the CPU, differentiates them and trains their parameters, through upstream ggml (the C tensor library behind llama.cpp), vendored in its CPU subset. It is a substrate, not a framework: tensors, explicit graphs, ggml’s autograd and optimisers, GGUF and safetensors for weights, a few modules, and a versioned C table for packages that build models on top. Its two consumers are zuflow, which trains and samples an event-sequence generator, and zukzeit, which runs pretrained time-series foundation models. Hard dependencies are the family’s zurand (random numbers, Imports and LinkingTo) and zujson (safetensors headers); nothing else. No GPU, no OpenMP, no system libraries.

.agents/design.md is the specification and outranks this file. .agents/roadmap.md is the stage plan with exit criteria. CLAUDE.md orients; the design decides.

Current state

Verified 2026-10-14: Stage 7 of the roadmap. ggml v0.26.0’s CPU subset is vendored and builds as CPU-dispatched variants (Stage 1). Stores and GGUF (Stage 2), graphs and operations (Stage 3), training through ggml-opt (Stage 4), zurand draws with fixed-order loss sums (Stage 5), modules and PyTorch fixtures (Stage 6), and one persistent, interruptible, fork-safe thread pool (Stage 7) exist; safetensors come in Stage 8. Patches P1, P2, P7, P8, P9 and P10 are vendored; none has an upstream pull request yet (design §9.3).

Stage tracking

Progress toward the next version is tracked as GitHub sub-issues, so the parent issue shows a progress bar such as “6 of 7”.

  • One parent issue per target version, titled with the bare version: v0.1.0 (#1).
  • One sub-issue per roadmap stage, titled as the roadmap titles it, for example Stage 3 — Graphs, operations, forward and validation, and linking to that section.
  • Every tracking issue carries the stage label, so it can be told apart from bug and feature issues and left out of open-issue counts.
  • Close a stage by merging its pull request. Put Closes #<n> in the body of the stage’s pull request. Never close a stage whose exit criteria are not met; record a deviation in the roadmap first.
  • The roadmap stays authoritative. The issues record which stages are done, not what a stage requires. Adding, removing or renaming a stage means editing the roadmap and the sub-issues in the same change.
  • Close the parent issue when CRAN accepts the version and it is tagged. Submission is tracked in CRAN-submission (#17).

Versioning

The package develops at 0.0.0.9000 and targets 0.1.0 for its first CRAN release. Set Version: 0.1.0 and the matching NEWS.md heading when the package enters Pre-flight. Bump to 0.1.0.9000 only after CRAN accepts it.

Until the first release the R API may change freely. The C table in inst/include/zulm.h (Stage 12) is different: zuflow and zukzeit build against it, so it follows the append-only rules of design §8 from the day it exists. zulm needs zurand on CRAN before it can be submitted; until then Remotes: pedrobtz/zurand stays in DESCRIPTION.

Commands

Run from the package root.

Rscript -e 'devtools::load_all()'                # compile src/ and load
Rscript -e 'devtools::document()'                # roxygen -> NAMESPACE, man/
Rscript -e 'devtools::test()'                    # full testthat suite
Rscript -e 'devtools::test(filter = "<name>")'   # one test file
Rscript -e 'devtools::test(shuffle = TRUE)'      # order independence
Rscript -e 'devtools::check()'                   # R CMD check
air format .                                     # format R sources

zurand is not on CRAN yet: install it from GitHub (pak::pak("pedrobtz/zurand")) before building.

Native build and vendored tree (occasional):

R CMD INSTALL --preclean .        # always --preclean after editing a header:
                                  # make does not track header dependencies
tools/vendor-ggml [TAG]           # re-vendor; tools/vendor-ggml --verify checks
tools/verify-ggml                 # offline: checksums and no diagnostic pragma
tools/gen-build                   # after vendoring or adding a glue source
tools/check-exports <libs dir>    # only R_init_ exported
Rscript tools/bench-variants.R x  # the 512^3 product on every usable variant

devtools::load_all() compiles at -O0; never measure speed on it, and reinstall with --preclean before measuring.

Architecture

Design §4 is the reference. In outline, as the stages build it:

  • R/ is the user surface, prefixed zl_; zulm_info() reports the build. Everything a user calls validates its arguments in R or in the C glue before ggml sees them.
  • src/ holds the C glue (prefix zlm_), a small C++ shim that turns ggml assertions into R errors (design §13.2), and src/ggml/, the vendored upstream tree, built once per ISA variant (design §13.1).
  • Variants: src/zlm_v/<set>/ holds generated wrapper translation units (one per ggml source) that include zlm_variant_begin.h, the source and zlm_variant_end.h; configure appends src/make/<arch>.mk to src/Makevars.in; src/install.libs.R installs every zulm_<variant> shared object. zulm.so itself is only the CPU probe; R/load.R loads the variant and calls its routines through zlm_call().
  • inst/include/zulm.h is the public C table, zulm_api_v1.

Invariants that are easy to break

  • No ggml assertion may reach abort(). Arguments ggml asserts on are validated first; what remains is caught by the abort callback and the shim (design §13.2). A test that reaches an assertion is a bug.
  • Nothing on a ggml pool thread calls R. Only the main thread touches R objects; errors cross as status codes.
  • Never write a compiler flag into Makevars, never compile a ggml source directly. Every ggml source goes through a zlm_v/ wrapper, which is what applies zlm_compat.h (no stdio, abort or _Exit may be linked) and the ISA pragmas. Regenerate with tools/gen-build.
  • A variant’s shared object is never unloaded. Objects it created are finalised by its code; R/load.R keeps every loaded variant, and a store made under one variant is zulm_stale_error under another.
  • C code raises R errors only through zlm_raise(), after freeing its own memory. zlm_raise() longjmps; anything malloc’d or any ggml or gguf context not owned by a protected external pointer leaks.
  • Store tensors never move. A store grows by batches; never reallocate a batch, because graphs hold its tensors’ addresses.
  • Never allocate a graph’s original nodes. zl_forward() runs a copy (zlm_dup.cpp); ggml-opt copies inherit data pointers, so an allocated original would make training read reused memory.
  • Every new operation needs its validation in validate() (zlm_graph.c): ggml asserts in builders and in kernels, and a kernel assertion during compute is fatal. Only f32 enters operations.
  • Training graphs stay unallocated and small. ggml-opt trains on the original nodes with static graphs and builds its forward graph at GGML_DEFAULT_GRAPH_SIZE (2048 nodes between parameters and loss); zl_grad() builds its own backward graph on a copy. Every operation on a gradient path needs a rule in the backward pre-check (zlm_train.c), or ggml aborts during ggml_build_backward_expand().
  • Results must not depend on the thread count. Reported losses are fixed-order sums of per-row values and random draws come from zurand under keys, never from a thread-local generator (design §6.5).

Testing conventions

  • Self-sufficient. Every test builds its own inputs inside the test_that() block. No file-scope objects.
  • Self-contained. Global state goes through withr::local_*(), randomised input through withr::local_seed(). Tests write only under tempdir().
  • Assert on condition classes, never message text. Use expect_error(..., class = "zulm_invalid_argument") and the other classes of design §10.
  • Order independence. devtools::test(shuffle = TRUE) is part of the definition of done.
  • Oracles before hand-written cases. Base-R implementations of each operation, central finite differences for gradients, and PyTorch fixtures written by tools/make-torch-reference.py (design §11).
  • Keep the suite inside the CRAN time budget. Long acceptance tests (the §1.1 model) run on CI only.

Definition of done

devtools::document() and devtools::check() clean, meaning 0 errors, 0 warnings and 0 notes. The one allowed note is “New submission” before the first release. devtools::test(shuffle = TRUE) green. gctorture(TRUE) clean when C changed. CI green on every leg. A user-facing change also needs a test, roxygen documentation and a NEWS.md entry.

Releasing to CRAN

  • CI is the pre-submission check. The pedrobtz/r-actions R CMD check runs --as-cran on the CRAN-like runners and containers, and it replaces win-builder, the macOS builder and R-hub. cran-comments.md lists the CI legs as its test environments.
  • Entering Pre-flight. The roadmap’s feature stages are done, the version is set as in Versioning, NEWS.md and cran-comments.md are written, and CI is green. Only submission work remains.
  • The pretest is automated and does not read cran-comments.md. Fix a NOTE instead of justifying it.
  • After acceptance, tag v0.1.0, publish the GitHub release, bump to 0.1.0.9000, and close the version’s parent issue.

Editing rules

  • roxygen comments are the source. Never edit man/ or NAMESPACE by hand.
  • Keep prose simple and short. One idea per sentence. en-GB spelling.
  • Wrap roxygen text at 80 characters and run air format . on R sources.
  • Use lower_snake_case; R functions take the zl_ prefix, internal native symbols zlm_, the public C table zulm_.
  • No hard runtime dependency beyond zurand and zujson without a recorded design decision.
  • Export and document public functions. Do not create roxygen topics for internal ones.

Continuous integration

Workflows come from pedrobtz/r-actions, pinned to @v1: r-cmd-check.yml (quick on pull requests, full on main, full on a pull request with the full-ci label; plus an x86-64 macOS runner), coverage.yml and vendor.yml, plus the pkgdown workflow. Local workflows: build-flags (fails on the non-portable-flag, pragma and compiled-code NOTEs and on any export besides R_init_), portability (the native hooks), measure (the §13.1 numbers, informational), vendor (re-vendors the tag and checks the generated build files) and interop (GGUF against upstream’s Python package). native-checks calls r-actions’ sanitizers, valgrind, LTO, gctorture, rchk, analyzers and cran-special workflows; rchk installs zurand from GitHub, and the analyzers report ggml’s own findings apart.

Small edits get a small run. The shared workflows look at the files a pull request changes, compared with its merge base:

  • Markdown only, such as README.md, NEWS.md or cran-comments.md, skips every check. Only coverage and the pkgdown site run.
  • DESCRIPTION or README.Rmd as well, and nothing else, adds one R CMD check on Ubuntu R-release.
  • Any other file runs everything.

Vendored native code

ggml’s CPU subset (MIT), pinned at tag v0.26.0, lives under src/ggml/, written by tools/vendor-ggml (design §9), which records tag, commit, patches, stripped pragmas and checksums in src/ggml/VERSION.

  • Never edit a file under src/ggml/. Changes go in tools/patches/, each with its reason and its upstream pull request (design §9.3).
  • CRAN’s compiled-code check applies to vendored code too. No stdout or stderr, no printf, abort or exit may be linked; upstream’s stdio is redirected to the log buffer and its diagnostic pragmas are stripped (design §9.2).
  • No -f, -m or -O flag in Makevars. ISA targets are chosen by pragmas in a force-included header (design §13.1, §13.4).

Commits and pull requests

Short, imperative, sentence-case commit subjects. Keep each commit focused. A pull request explains the user-visible outcome and the rationale, links related issues, lists the checks that were run and the tests that were skipped, and flags platform-sensitive or vendored changes. Performance claims need evidence.
